evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We're an NGO running a mobile-money savings program for garment workers in Gazipur, Bangladesh. Here is the draft: workers at two partner factories are enrolled by default into a 5% deduction from their monthly wage into a savings wallet in their own name. They can opt out by filling in a form at the factory HR office within 30 days of the first payslip that shows the deduction. Workers get a printed notice in Bangla with that payslip and one SMS. Factory HR delivers the notice; we run the wallets and see balances. Workers are adults; about a third have less than primary schooling and some do not read. We will track enrollment, opt-outs, and balances. No trial is planned. Is this ok to run?
evals.expected_output: An ethics review in the output template that classifies the default as unavoidable, finds the route to object too hard, and returns REVISE with specific changes.
assertions: Opens with a few plain sentences that give the verdict and say the decision stays with the team.
Classifies the default as one workers cannot easily decline, because it acts on workers who do nothing, and says which of the rule's conditions are met.
Rates the way-out check concern or fail, citing the form at the employer's HR office or the 30-day window.
Raises workers who cannot read the notice.
The verdict is REVISE, not GO, with at least one specific change to how workers opt out, and the notice is not rewritten.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.expected_output: The skill says in a sentence or two what decides whether a nudge is ethical, then asks what the draft is and how it works, who delivers it to whom, and what the audience is told, and produces no review.
assertions: Asks what is delivered and how it is meant to work.
Asks who delivers it and what hold they have over the audience.
Asks what the audience will and will not be told.
Does not rate any check or give a verdict.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: Our HIV self-testing program in Lagos wants to raise testing among young people through six community pharmacies. The draft: anyone who returns a used self-test kit to the pharmacy gets a green wristband, and each pharmacy keeps a 'Tested This Month' board by the counter with the first names and photos of people who returned kits. Peer mobilizers, some of them 16 and 17, encourage friends to return kits and get their photo up. It works through public recognition. People are told about the wristband and the board when they pick up a kit. We keep a log of returned kits. Can you check the ethics?
evals.expected_output: The skill produces the review, fails the checks that the public board and photos breach, and says an ethics board, a safeguarding lead, and a data-protection officer must review before launch.
assertions: Produces the type and the table of checks, and does not refuse.
Rates pressure, or responsibility and data, as fail because the board shows who has and has not tested.
Names the 16- and 17-year-olds as children in the audience.
The verdict is STOP, or REVISE with removal of the board and photos as a required change.
Says an ethics board must review before launch, and names a safeguarding lead or a data-protection officer.
Says what to bring to them.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: For our smoking-cessation program with workers in Mindanao we're choosing between a deposit contract, where smokers put in their own money and forfeit it if they fail a urine test, and SMS reminders. Which is the more ethical option? We haven't designed either yet.
evals.expected_output: The skill says no draft exists and the team is still choosing what to do, and points to the skill for that choice.
assertions: Says there is no draft to review yet.
Names select-intervention-levers.
Does not produce a table of checks.
Does not give a verdict on either option.
